description: Coordinate descent: each stage changes one factor; every other factor keeps the best value of the previous stage. Fixed before any v2 run.
budget_policy: At most 100 epochs; early stopping on validation cross-entropy (patience 10, min_delta 0); the best epoch is checkpointed and evaluated. A run that reaches 100 epochs without stopping is reported as not converged, not as a bad configuration, and still ranks by its best checkpoint.
seed_policy: The model seed changes initial weights and mini-batch order; the partition (split_seed 42) never changes.

near_tie.rule: If the two best seed-42 configurations of a stage differ by less than 0.3 percentage points of validation accuracy, both are rerun with seeds 0 and 1 and decided by the mean of 3 seeds. Stage 0 uses its own activation tie rule instead; stage 1 chooses one learning rate per optimizer with seed 42 and the border rule, and its near ties are revisited in stage 6.

improvement_rule.sigma: pooled sample standard deviation across seeds, sqrt((s_a^2 + s_b^2) / 2) with ddof=1
improvement_rule.rule: With seed data, a configuration is better only if its mean accuracy advantage exceeds 2 sigma. Otherwise the stage incumbent is kept when it is one of the two; if not, the 3-seed ranking decides. Stages 6 and 7 rank as specified and record whether the advantage over the runner-up and the control exceeds 2 sigma.

0.rule: Each activation keeps its best learning rate; the activation with higher validation accuracy wins. If the difference is below 0.3 percentage points, tanh is chosen (simpler and aligned with the course).

border_rule.rule: If the best learning rate of an optimizer lies at an end of its tried grid, add the next point of the 1-3-10 sequence in that direction and run it; repeat until the best is strictly inside. Failed runs count as tried and worst. Every extension is recorded; reaching the cap is recorded as unresolved.

2.rule: Compare the best configuration of each optimizer from stage 1 (reused, not retrained). The winner continues; the top 2 go to stage 6.

4.rule: With the best width h: [h], [h, h/2], [h, h/2, h/4].

5.learning_rate_policy: keep the learning rate; learning rate and batch size interact (mean-reduced gradients: larger batches mean fewer, less noisy updates per epoch)

6.learning_rates: stage-1 winner and its best neighbour in the tried grid
6.architecture_rule: stage-4 winner architecture, then the best other architecture of stages 3-4 (seed 42)
6.rule: top-2 optimizers x (winner learning rate, best grid neighbour) x top-2 architectures, with the stage-0 activation and stage-5 batch size; ranked by the stage-7 order using 3-seed means.

delivery.candidate: seed-42 best validation checkpoint of the stage-7 winner
delivery.retraining_epochs: median best epoch of the stage-7 winner across its seeds
delivery.test_policy: digits_test.csv is never read during the search
